Hi Priya / Rahul,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — great to hear about FintechCo's plans to expand the payments product and the sensitivity around transaction-level data. Per our discussion, I wanted to recap the key items and propose next steps so we can move the SOC/DPA and technical deep-dive forward.

Recap (short):
- You need clarity on what Redwood logs (request/response payloads, headers, trace IDs) and how long those logs are retained.
- Concern about PII appearing in request or response text and whether Redwood redacts/masks it automatically.
- Requirement to produce SOC2 evidence and to execute a Data Processing Addendum (DPA).
- For Dedicated/Private deployments you asked about configurable retention and network/PKI controls.

What Redwood provides (high level):
- Request/response logs: used for troubleshooting and observability; default hosted retention is 30 days but can be shortened or disabled for enterprise customers.
- Sensitive data handling: we support pattern-based automatic redaction (configurable), header redaction rules, and optional suppression/hashing of trace IDs in logs.
- Dedicated/Private: longer-term retention and audit logging policies are configurable; on-prem options allow you to control the persistence layer entirely.
- Compliance artifacts: SOC2 evidence is available via a secure portal; we'll share the specific artifacts you requested (scope: logging, access controls, change management).

Attachments: I attached a short summary (redaction_controls.pdf) with the default behaviors and admin controls. I'll also pull the SOC2 pack and share via secure link.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Technical deep-dive with Dev & Dylan to walk your infra/security team through redaction knobs and sample logs (30–45 min).
2) We will send SOC2 artifacts + DPA draft by EOD tomorrow.
3) If helpful, we can provide a short PoC (masked logs export) for your security team.

Proposed times for technical deep-dive: Wed 6/2 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 6/3 9:00–10:00 PT. Which works best for you?

Thanks —

Hi Priya — great questions, answers below (high level). Dev and Dylan are cc'd and will join the technical call to walk through implementation and config examples.

1) Request/response persistence: by default in our hosted offering we persist request/response payloads to a secure logging store for up to 30 days to support debugging, rate limiting analysis, and quality monitoring. However, before persistence we can apply configurable redaction rules (pattern-based and ML-assisted detectors) to remove common PII types (SSNs, credit card numbers, email addresses) and customer-specified sensitive fields. For customers that require no payload persistence we offer:
   - Option A: disable request/response payload persistence entirely (no logs stored)
   - Option B: persist only hashed/scrubbed payloads (we replace matched patterns with deterministic hashes)

2) Headers & trace IDs: header redaction rules can be applied at ingestion (drop or mask headers like Authorization, Cookie, X-Forwarded-For). Trace IDs are persisted by default to correlate requests but we can hash or suppress them in stored logs per tenant policy to prevent cross-referencing.

3) Retention controls: default hosted retention = 30 days. For enterprise customers (Dedicated/Private) retention windows are configurable down to 0 days; we can also provide rolling export hooks if you need to ship logs to your SIEM instead of storing them in Redwood.

4) SOC2 & DPA: we'll upload the requested SOC2 evidence for logging, change management, and access reviews to a secure artifact portal (link below). We can also circulate our standard DPA for review; we typically sign a DPA as part of the contract or via the HubSpot legal flow.

Attachments/links: redaction_controls.pdf (attached) + SOC2 bundle to be uploaded to the secure portal: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example_redaction_controls
